summary: Macau follows the Portuguese model: children and other close family have a protected share that a will cannot override (about half the estate for one child, two thirds for two or more, per a secondary source). The Hague Trusts Convention applies through China, and Law 15/2022 gives an onshore trust law since December 2022. Foundations exist only for social-interest purposes.
reserved_share: Spouse, descendants and ascendants are forced heirs under the Civil Code (Book V). A law-firm source says one child is protected for half the estate and two or more for two thirds; I did not confirm the articles or the spouse and parent shares.
foreign_law_note: Macau's private international law applies the deceased's personal law, believed to be nationality. A 2019 Court of Second Instance ruling (Proc. 66/2015) held that a foreign judgment excluding forced heirs was not contrary to Macau public order because Macau law did not govern the succession. I did not read the article text.
trust_note: HCCH: China's continuation covers Hong Kong and Macau, so the Convention is in force for Macau. Trust Law 15/2022 (in force 1 December 2022): only licensed entities such as banks, insurers and asset managers can be trustees; the law has no specific tax treatment. Civil Code foundations (fundacoes) are for social-interest purposes, not family benefit (not confirmed in text).
open_questions: Confirm the Civil Code articles and fractions of the legitima (spouse, ascendants, one child, several children).
Confirm the conflict article for succession and whether nationality law governs a foreign resident.
Confirm foundation provisions in the Civil Code arts. 158-168 and any private use.
